correctness.rationale: With i deletions and j retained letters so far, the next source letter has phase i+j modulo q, while the next required deleted letter has phase i. Pairwise distinct letters force all deletions to occur at retained counts j divisible by q. The intervening retained blocks are rotations determined by i modulo q. To obtain given phases, the minimal gaps are the least residues of consecutive phase differences, from initial phase 0 and with a return to terminal phase 0. Their sum is q times the number of descents including the last return; any excess full periods may be put in a gap. The cut into q-letter blocks is unique, including the empty case. For an independent check of the polynomial, count weakly sorted r-tuples of integers in [0,qj] by their residues s_i modulo q. Their quotients must increase by one at each internal descent and the final quotient is <= j-1 if s_r>0. Removing those shifts gives binom(j-d(s)+r,r) possibilities for j>=d(s), zero otherwise. Summation over phases and then j gives F_{q,r}(z)/(1-z)^(r+1)=sum_{j>=0}binom(qj+r,r)z^j. Summing in r by the geometric series gives the stated rational form; the coefficient of z^k in F_{q,r}/(1-z) yields the finite count. This is a classification of distinct linear remainder words for whole powers, not embedding multiplicity or cyclic equivalence of the remainders.
correctness.reproduction: For q=2,3,4 and m=1,...,4 with every 0<=k<=m, take P=(0,1,...,q-1). For each subset of qk positions in P^m, keep its complement if the deleted letters spell P^k; compare the deduplicated complements with the rotation-block products filtered by d<=k. An independent implementation matched all 42 sets, checking 19308 masks. A separate enumeration of all phase words for q=2,3,4 and r=0,...,4 matched the 15 formal polynomial cases and the finite count in all 42 set cases. The frozen checker and stored output are evidence, not executed in this review; the finite replay is not the proof for arbitrary exponents.

evidence: The bounded-digit theorem has the same linear, distinct-letter setup, same rotation blocks and the same source/target powers after its m is identified with the frozen r. It filters on E=s_1+sum (s_{i+1}-s_i mod q)<=qk. If g counts internal descents, the residues telescope to E=qg+s_r. Therefore ceil(E/q)=g+1_{s_r>0}=d for nonempty words, and both costs are zero for the empty word.

For q=2, descents 1 to 0 plus the terminal indicator count precisely the runs of phase 1, or maximal runs of ba blocks. The alternating-word theorem gives that same membership criterion for all r and k.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The two checked indexed results together classify all allowed instances of the frozen complement set. Adding the final return to phase 0 merely rounds the cost up to a multiple of q; the inequality against qk cannot distinguish the two formulations.

evidence: The exact q>=3 indexed count is the coefficient through degree qk of (1+x+...+x^(q-1))^r. Equivalently it is [x^(qk)](1-x^q)^r/(1-x)^(r+1), whose binomial expansion is the frozen alternating sum.

The q=2 indexed count is sum_{i<=k}binom(r+1,2i), which counts the same phase words; its finite differences are the same descent coefficients. The stride-q binomial series is the standard Veronese construction on (1-z)^(-r-1).

originality.rationale: Verified distinct indexed statements already cover the mathematical content. The bounded-digit theorem gives the same classification and all counts for q>=3, and the alternating-word run theorem covers q=2. Their equivalence uses an exact telescoping change of cost, not parameter resemblance. Every claimed enumerator then follows mechanically from the bounded-digit counts, including the formal descent series. This is a finding of equivalent coverage in the checked material, not a conclusion about which author or version was first: the equivalent catalog paths have later displayed dates than the assigned frozen path, and that observation alone neither establishes priority nor changes the statement comparison.
residual_risks: The displayed index dates and mirror evidence do not establish research priority. The verdict is about demonstrable equivalence, not misconduct or earlier authorship.
